LESSON: WRITING 4.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING : A REPLY TO A FRIENDLY LETTER

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing : A Reply to a Friendly Letter
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing : A Reply to a Friendly Letter, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: How do you communicate with people who are far away? 2. Why do we write letters?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the components of a friendly letter from a sample letter,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing : A Reply to a Friendly Letter in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write a friendly letter using the correct format for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing : A Reply to a Friendly Letter in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. judge the appropriateness of words, phrases and sentences used in friendly letters. Learner is guided to: • Read a sample friendly letter with peers and pick out the parts such as address, salutation, date, complimentary close among others, • Write a reply to a sample friendly letter using the correct format. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials, alternative functional parts of the body, use assistive technology or type. • Proofread/edit the letter collaboratively, • Present the edited version to other groups, • Search for more examples of friendly letters on the internet while collaborating with peers. , 1. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing : A Reply to a Friendly Letter together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Love is enhanced as learners read and write and reply friendly letters to each other.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills Education: Effective communication is developed as the learner learns how to write a friendly letter.

Link to other Subjects:

The learner applies the skills and knowledge derived from letter writing to similar concept learnt in Kiswahili.
